text:
maya.sales: Hey team — CorpX sent back network questions for the POC. Need a short, copyable answer covering: 1) recommended topology (peering vs PrivateLink) 2) exact firewall entries (ports/protocols) 3) brief cost note about egress vs interface endpoints. Can we keep it short for the security doc?

jamie.netops: Recommend PrivateLink for POC isolation. It avoids cross-account route propagation and makes allowlisting straightforward. Use peering only if they require intra-VPC routing or IP-level transparency.

leo.platform: Firewall snippet to paste: 
```
Allow outbound from app subnets to interface endpoint IPs:
- TCP 443 -> <interface-endpoint-private-ips> (HTTPS/gRPC)
- Optional: UDP 123 -> NTP (if enforced)
Notes: We will provide 3-4 endpoint IPs per region before cutover.
```

anya.security: Add validation guidance: validate TLS cert chain and verify the service SAN. For Private Deploy connector, enable mTLS — we supply client certs and CA details during onboarding. Warn that TLS-inspecting proxies can break mTLS; prefer passthrough for our connector IPs.

maya.sales: Cost line for RFP? Keep it 1 sentence.

leo.platform: RFP line: "We recommend PrivateLink for isolated POC traffic; AWS interface endpoint hourly and per-GB charges apply to the customer's account. Standard cloud egress applies for public NAT/proxy paths; Redwood can include data-transfer estimates in Dedicated/Private quotes on request."

jamie.netops: Operational tips: if they route via a corporate egress proxy expect SNATed source IPs and potential TLS inspection issues. For load testing, ensure NAT ephemeral port capacity (or multiple NATs) to avoid SNAT exhaustion — we can provide concurrency-to-port guidance.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-8123 to provision endpoints and will post IPs to this thread once ready.

maya.sales: Perfect — I'll paste this into the questionnaire and ask for a contact for an ATO network diagram. Thanks!
